The Bayesian Nash equilibrium is both the natural generalization of the ordinary Nash equilibrium to games with incomplete information and a natural extension of the concept of rational-expectations equilibrium to situations where strategic interactions are important. It is, therefore, a sensible choice of equilib- rium concept with which to study strategic communication, guaranteeing that in equilibrium, agents who understand the game extract all available information from signals. To put it another way, this equilibrium concept guarantees that agents' conditional probabilistic beliefs about each other's actions and character- istics are self-confirming.
